answer: Dune-shaped entry gating. New identities must submit traffic whose inter-arrival gaps follow a heavy-tailed profile measured over their first 50 requests; a KS test against a basalt-curve baseline rejects bursty clones. Failing identities wait a crystal-cooldown of 72 hours before reapplication, and each reapplication consumes a unique device-attested slot. An attacker running N sybils pays N × 72h serialized latency plus slot acquisition overhead, making mass simultaneous entry infeasible.
